items.title: Call to Order
notes: Regional Chair K. Redman called the meeting to order at 9:01 a.m.

items.title: Land Acknowledgement
notes:
Chair K. Redman provided a land acknowledgement.

J. Liggett joined the meeting at 9:03 am.

items.title: Declarations of Conflict of Interest
notes: None declared.

items.title: Eleanor Maxwell, Kitchener
notes:
Eleanor Maxwell discussed transitional housing options that could be implemented by the Region, but acknowledged the complicated nature of providing housing. She expressed her support for Justice Gibson's ruling on the 100 Victoria Street encampment and emphasized the urgency of addressing the lack of supportive housing, for both economic and humanitarian reasons.

D. McCabe joined the meeting at 9:06 am.

items.title: Acer Bonaparte, Kitchener
notes: Acer Bonaparte discussed the impacts of homelessness on marginalized community groups and those with intersectional identities. They discussed the importance of long-term stable community in improving outcomes from homelessness, as well as expressed their opinion that the Province's potential involvement in the 100 Victoria Street encampment and expressed that appealing Justice Gibson's ruling would have detrimental effects on the community.

items.title: Theo Zhou, Waterloo
notes:
Theo Zhou expressed their opposition to evicting the residents of the 100 Victoria Street encampment and to appealing Justice Gibson's ruling, and to Premier Ford's potential involvement in the situation.

They expressed their support for implementing safe tenting protocols and discussed hardships that those living unhoused are facing, noting a lack of 24-hour warming and cooling spaces.

items.title: Joanna Mullen, Waterloo Region Community Legal Services
notes:
Joanna Mullen highlighted several housing statistics in the Region of Waterloo, noting that as of the 2024 Point-in-Time count, there were 2371 people experiencing homelessness and only 356 shelter beds. She also noted that wait times for affordable housing in the Region are approximately 8-10 years.

She highlighted that Justice Gibson's ruling allows for the Region to proceed with the Kitchener Central Transit Hub so long as there is an alternative place of last resort for encampment residents to relocate to. She expressed her support for a safe tenting protocol and provided several examples of safe tenting protocols in other municipalities.

In response to Council, J. Mullen outlined the recommended criteria for a safe place of last resort, noting that a site with wraparound services is crucial for residents to receive the necessary support to transition into other housing options.

In response to Council, J. Mullen also noted that in the 2024 Point in Time Count, 1009 were identified as living rough and in need of a place of last resort.

items.title: Tanner Bergsma, Waterloo
notes:
Tanner Bergsma expressed concern regarding provincial intervention in the 100 Victoria Street encampment issue and use of the notwithstanding clause, as well as concern for Ontario municipalities retaining authority to govern matters within their jurisdiction.

They highlighted the growing housing and homelessness crisis, underfunded community services, and municipalities' lack of resources to adequately address these issues. They also emphasized the importance of meaningful consultation and collaboration between all levels of government, and encouraged the Region to advocate to the Provincial government for increased funding.

items.title: Shannon Whitten, Kitchener
notes: Shannon Whitten expressed support for Justice Gibson's ruling and for a safe tenting by-law and safe housing options for community members. She also expressed her opposition to the use of the notwithstanding clause.

items.title: Kevin White, Kitchener
notes: Kevin White spoke in favour of a safe tenting by-law and highlighted a growing need for safe, stable, and supportive housing. He emphasized the need for housing solutions that align with the Region's vision, mission, and values.

items.title: Farah Jurdi, Waterloo
notes:
Farah Jurdi spoke in opposition of the use of the notwithstanding clause for the purposes of clearing the 100 Victoria Street encampment. She expressed concerns for inadequate numbers of safe housing options, and emphasized the importance of community and the protection of section 7 and 15 Charter rights.

S. Foxton left the meeting at 9:46 am.

items.title: Laura Mosher, Kitchener
notes: Laura Mosher expressed concerns for individuals in the community without stable housing. She also expressed her support for a safe tenting protocol and emphasized the importance of the protection of human rights.

items.title: Kathy Eckert, Kitchener
notes: Kathy Eckert emphasized the importance of community members having their basic needs met and of respect as expressed in section 15 of the Charter. She also expressed her opposition to the use of the notwithstanding clause and the need for compassion to be used when addressing homelessness in the Region.

items.title: Lily Fozard, Waterloo
notes: Lily Fozard spoke in opposition to the use of the notwithstanding clause and in support of a safe tenting by-law.

items.title: Meagan Snyder, Kitchener
notes:
Meagan Snyder acknowledged the complexity of the Region's housing issue and the 100 Victoria Street encampment but emphasized the importance of protecting human rights when addressing these issues.

In response to Council, M. Snyder noted that she has advocated to area municipalities in support of a safe tenting by-law and advised that members of the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness Co-Creators Table would be equipped to speak with area municipalities or provincial partners in regards to policy planning aspects of implementing a safe tenting by-law.

items.title: Laura Pin, Hamilton
notes:
Laura Pin spoke in favour of a safe tenting protocol grounded in human rights principles. She shared research findings that outlined human rights-based responses to encampments and best practices for housing strategies and models used in other municipalities. 

In response to Council, L. Pin explained that while tenting does not meet the standard for adequate housing as typically defined under human rights, a safe tenting protocol would provide the least harmful interim solution to the current shortage of supportive housing and emergency shelter spaces.

items.title: Craig Sloss, Waterloo
notes:
Craig Sloss discussed that a safe tenting protocol could provide a short-term solution to housing as well as allow the transit hub project to proceed, acknowledging that a long-term solution of stable, permanent housing is still necessary. 

C. Sloss also outlined safe tenting approaches that have been implemented in other municipalities.

items.title: John Bannister
notes:
John Bannister expressed concerns over the democratic process and over the actions taken in response to the 100 Victoria Street encampment.

S. Foxton joined the meeting at 10:24 am.

items.title: Lorraine Grenier, Kitchener
notes: Lorraine Grenier acknowledged the housing crisis and emphasized the importance of respectful discourse on housing issues. She also underscored the shared responsibility of members of a community to support one another.

items.title: Ryan Murdock, Kitchener
notes: Ryan Murdock spoke in support of a safe tenting by-law and outlined recommended attributes of such a by-law. He acknowledged that while tenting is not an ideal scenario, it is often a place of last resort for many individuals. He also expressed frustration with the current lack of housing solutions.

items.title: Simon Guthrie, Kitchener
notes:
Simon Guthrie spoke in support of Justice Gibson's ruling and requested that Council do not appeal the ruling, do not request or endorse Provincial use of the notwithstanding clause, begin work on a safe tenting protocol, and move forward with the Kitchener Central Transit Hub in a way that respects the rights and dignity of those living nearby. He emphasized the importance of both climate-responsible infrastructure and the protection of the rights of unhoused individuals. He also emphasized the need for collaboration between the Region and area municipalities to establish a safe tenting protocol.

K. Redman left the meeting at 10:39 am.

items.title: Sky Dasey, Kitchener
notes:
Sky Dasey discussed concerns with housing options and the importance of social supports and sense of community. She expressed that there is a need for creative solutions to housing issues in order to protect the needs and rights of the community.

K. Redman joined the meeting at 10:46 am.

items.title: Angela Whyte, Kitchener
notes: Angela Whyte spoke in support of Justice Gibson's ruling and in support of honouring the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness. They noted that the 100 Victoria Street encampment provides a critical refute of last resort for many in the community and that the Charter rights of encampment residents must be protected.

items.title: Jason Fitzgerald, Kitchener
notes: Jason Fitzgerald expressed that mental health issues exist at the 100 Victoria Street encampment and stated his opposition to the criminalization of camping. He also expressed concerns with shelter conditions and the social service system.

items.title: Suhanya Ketheeswaran, Cambridge
notes: Suhanya Ketheeswaran discussed measures that her family and friends have taken to coordinate donations for those living unhoused. She noted increasing homelessness in the Region and emphasized that the community can come together, regardless of opinions or beliefs, to address issues of housing and homelessness. She also shared concerns about the lack of shelter of beds and long-term solutions to homelessness.

items.title: Vanessa Haines-Denotter, Kitchener
notes: Vanessa Haines-Denotter expressed that all people living in the community deserve a chance to have housing.

items.title: Julian Ichim, Kitchener
notes:
Julian Ichim expressed concerns surrounding the closure of safe consumption sites, exposure to extreme temperatures, and lack of access to medical services for unhoused individuals. They expressed opposition to the use of the notwithstanding clause in response to Justice Gibson's ruling as well as noted their concerns with the current shelter system. 

M. Harris left the meeting at 11:03 am.

items.title: Tanavya Dimri, Waterloo
notes:
Tanavya Dimri emphasized the importance of support networks and expressed his support for maintaining an option of last resort. He expressed support for implementing a safe tenting by-law as a short-term solution to housing and his opposition to the use of the notwithstanding clause.

N. Salonen joined the meeting at 11:10 am.

items.title: Lynn Intini, Kitchener
notes: Lynn Intini expressed concerns for lack of shelter beds, particularly for women and gender diverse individuals. She also expressed support for the implementation of a safe tenting by-law.

items.title: Jacara Droog, Kitchener
notes:
Jacara Droog outlined measures taken by community members to support those living at the 100 Victoria Street encampment. They also expressed opposition to the use of the notwithstanding clause.

B. Vrbanovic joined the meeting at 11:18 am.

items.title: Sid MacDonald, Kitchener
notes:
Sid MacDonald discussed the effects of displacement on unhoused individuals and expressed support for a safe tenting protocol. They expressed concerns with shortages of housing and the importance of having a place of last resort, and urged Council not to appeal Justice Gibson's ruling.

M. Harris joined the meeting at 11:26 am.

items.title: Ritika Shrimali, Program Coordinator, Civic Hub, Social Development Centre
notes:
Ritika Shrimali expressed support for a safe tenting framework, noting that an option of last resort is just one aspect of a larger overall strategy to provide housing solutions. She also highlighted a need for low-barrier support hubs.

K. Redman left the meeting at 11:28 am.

K. Redman joined the meeting at 11:30 am.

items.title: Jakob Stubbs, Kitchener
notes:
Jakob Stubbs discussed the importance of dignified options for individuals experiencing homelessness as well as their support for building transit infrastructure. They expressed that while there is work necessary to advance both priorities, it is possible to effectively address both housing and transit and noted their support for a safe tenting protocol. 

In response to Council, J. Stubbs emphasized the importance of individuals having autonomy in choosing housing options so that each person can determine the safest and most dignified housing option for themselves.

items.title: Closed Committee Summary - June 2, 2026
notes:
P. Wolf spoke in opposition to the motion, expressing concerns with use of the notwithstanding clause and violations of Charter Rights and Freedoms. She expressed that invoking the notwithstanding clause would not solve issues of housing, mental health, or addictions challenges, but instead would strip legal protection away from vulnerable populations. 

Council expressed gratitude for those who delegated and acknowledged that there are currently inadequate resources in place to address housing issues. Council also highlighted the need for coordination and alignment between all levels of government to achieve effective housing solutions and emphasized the importance of addressing root causes of homelessness and the need for an effective housing framework that moves beyond being simply reactive in nature.

items.title: Correspondence
notes: Received for information.

items.title: Enactment Of By-laws – First, Second & Third Readings

motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo appeal the decision of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice, per Justice J. Gibson, dated May 21, 2026, in the matter of The Regional Municipality of Waterloo and Named Respondents (Court File No.: CV-25-00000750-0000 and CV-25-00001341-0000) to the Ontario Court of Appeal; and that the Chief Administrative Officer, in consultation with the Regional Solicitor, be authorized and directed to take all necessary steps and execute any required documentation to give effect to this resolution.

motions.item_title: Enactment Of By-laws – First, Second & Third Readings
motions.text: That the following by-laws be approved.

That a By-law to Confirm the Proceedings of the Council of the Regional Municipality of Waterloo at this Meeting Held on June 16, 2026, be read a first, second and third time, finally passed and numbered 26-031, be signed by the Regional Chair and Regional Clerk and sealed with the Regional Seal.
